summary: This document describes OSPF-TE extensions that support GMPLS control of Optical Transport Networks as specified in ITU-T G.709 (2012 edition). It extends mechanisms defined in RFC 4203.

eli5.summary: Optical networks have new kinds of boxes for carrying data. This teaches routers to announce and track those boxes.

subtitle: How OSPF learns which optical containers, slots and bandwidths each OTN link can switch, so GMPLS can plan paths across them.

tldr.problem: G.709 (2012) optical networks added new fixed and flexible ODU containers, two sizes of tributary slot and several multiplexing layers. The existing GMPLS routing encoding in RFC 4203 could not describe all of that.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7138 defines a new switching capability value, OTN-TDM (110), and two Bandwidth sub-TLVs carried in the Interface Switching Capability Descriptor. They list each container type, its multiplexing stages, slot granularity and the bandwidth left at each priority.
tldr.outcome: OSPF-TE nodes can now advertise OTN capabilities in a compact form, and path computation can use them. The extension has no direct effect on IP routing.

today: RFC 7138 is a Proposed Standard, published in March 2014, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends RFC 4203 and works with RFC 7139, which defines the signaling side and the Signal Type values.

sections.title: Why OTN Needs New Routing Encoding
sections.content:
ITU-T G.709, the standard for the Optical Transport Network (OTN), was published in a 2012 edition that adds new fixed and flexible ODU (Optical channel Data Unit) containers. It includes two types of tributary slot (1.25 Gbps and 2.5 Gbps), supports several multiplexing relationships such as an ODUj multiplexed into an ODUk (j<k), and adds the ODUflex service type.

To advertise this information in routing, RFC 7138 provides an OTN-specific encoding for GMPLS OSPF-TE as defined in RFC 4203. The reader is expected to know RFC 7062 (OTN overview) and RFC 7096 (the information model). Routing for the optical channel (wavelength) layer is out of scope; RFC 6163 and RFC 6566 cover it.
sections.eli5: Optical networks got new kinds of boxes and new ways of stacking them. The old announcements had no words for them, so this RFC adds the words.

sections.title: Multiplexing Trees and Notation
sections.content:
In a GMPLS OTN network, each OTUk (Optical channel Transport Unit-k) can be seen as a component link, and each component link can carry one or more types of ODUj (j<k). OSPF-TE must be able to advertise the termination and switching capabilities of each ODUj and ODUk/OTUk, plus the related multiplexing capabilities.

The RFC calls a multiplexing hierarchy a multiplexing tree. Its root is always the server ODUk/OTUk, and every other supported container hangs below it with finer granularity down to the leaves. In the RFC's example, ODU4 is the root, ODU3 and ODU2 are multiplexed directly into it, ODU2 and ODU0 are leaves of the ODU3 branch, and ODUflex and ODU0 are leaves of the ODU2 branch. Each path from leaf to root, such as ODUflex->ODU2->ODU4, is one multiplexing capability.
sections.eli5: Think of nesting dolls: small boxes go inside medium boxes, which go inside one big box. The tree is the picture of which boxes fit inside which.

sections.title: Representing OTN Links as TE-Links
sections.content:
G.709 ODUk/OTUk links are represented as TE-Links in the GMPLS traffic engineering topology so that ODUj layer switching can be supported. An OTUk physical link can be modeled as a TE-Link, giving one-hop TE-Links between OTN switches.

It is also possible to create TE-Links that span more than one hop by creating forwarding adjacencies (FAs) between non-adjacent nodes. As in the one-hop case, multiple-hop TE-Links advertise the ODU switching capability.
sections.eli5: A TE-Link is a road on the planner's map. It can be one short road between neighbours, or a shortcut that skips the towns in between.

sections.title: The OTN-TDM ISCD and Bandwidth Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
RFC 7138 adds a new Switching Capability value to the Interface Switching Capability Descriptor (ISCD) from RFC 4203: 110, OTN-TDM capable. Implementations MUST use Switching Capability = OTN-TDM and Encoding Type = G.709 ODUk (Digital Path) as defined in RFC 4328, for both fixed and flexible ODUs. The MAX LSP Bandwidth field is used as in RFC 4203, in bytes per second in IEEE floating point format.

The technology-specific part of the ISCD holds a variable number of Bandwidth sub-TLVs. Type 1 (Unreserved Bandwidth for fixed containers) MUST appear once per fixed container, and Type 2 (Unreserved/MAX LSP Bandwidth for flexible containers) once per variable container. Each is identified by a Signal Type defined in RFC 7139.

For ODUflex, three Signal Types are allowed: 20 for ODUflex(CBR), 21 for ODUflex(GFP-F) resizable and 22 for ODUflex(GFP-F) non-resizable. Each MUST be advertised in its own Type 2 sub-TLV, but if both 21 and 22 are supported, only 21 is advertised because it implies support for 22.

A single ISCD MAY cover bundled or unbundled links with homogeneous multiplexing hierarchies and the same tributary slot granularity. A different ISCD MUST be used for each different muxing tree and each different granularity in the TE-Link. A receiver that finds a badly formatted sub-TLV SHOULD log the problem and MUST NOT use that sub-TLV for path computation.
sections.eli5: Each link posts a standard form. The form says what kinds of boxes it handles and, for each kind, how many it can still take.

sections.title: Sub-TLV Fields in Detail
sections.content:
Both sub-TLV types start with a 16-bit Type and 16-bit Length, then Signal Type (8 bits) and Num of stages (8 bits), a flags byte, and a Priority bitmap (8 bits). The flags byte holds T (can be terminated), S (can be switched), a 3-bit TSG and 3 reserved bits. T and S cannot both be 0.

TSG (tributary slot granularity) takes these values: 0 ignored (used for non-multiplexed signal types), 1 for 1.25 Gbps or 2.5 Gbps (interfaces configured for the G.798 fallback procedures), 2 for 2.5 Gbps only (such as RFC 4328 interfaces), and 3 for 1.25 Gbps only. Values 4 to 7 are reserved.

The Priority bitmap marks which of the priority levels 0 (leftmost, highest) to 7 (rightmost, lowest) are advertised, and at least one MUST be, normally priority 0. After it come one Stage field (8 bits) per multiplexing stage, ordered from the lowest-order ODU to the highest, followed by padding to keep 32-bit alignment.

Type 1 then carries, for each advertised priority, a 16-bit count of unreserved ODUj containers, padded when the number of priorities is odd. Type 2 carries a 32-bit Unreserved Bandwidth and a 32-bit MAX LSP Bandwidth per priority, in bytes per second as IEEE floating point. MAX LSP Bandwidth MUST account for the HO OPUk bit rate tolerance: (# available TSs) x (ODTUk.ts nominal bit rate) x (1 - HO OPUk bit rate tolerance).
sections.eli5: The form has tick boxes for what a link can do with each box type, a slot size, and a count of free boxes at each importance level. Counting boxes takes less room than writing out sizes.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The non-normative examples in Section 5 show the encoding at work. On an OTU4 link with priorities 0, 2, 4 and 7 and the hierarchy ODU1->ODU2->ODU3->ODU4, the MAX LSP Bandwidth at priority 2 starts at 100 Gbps. After an ODU3 is set up at priority 2 it drops to 40 Gbps, and after an ODU2 is set up at priority 4 the lower-priority levels drop to 10 Gbps.

Other examples cover different T, S and TSG settings, two interfaces with different slot granularities (which need two ISCDs), ODUflex advertisement, single-stage and multi-stage muxing, bundled links and component links with non-homogeneous hierarchies. For ODUflex, the RFC notes that unreserved bandwidth does not show how the free slots are laid out. With 50 Gbps unreserved on link A and 10 Gbps on link B, three 10 Gbps ODUflex LSPs are certain to fit only once on B, and probably, not certainly, twice on A.
sections.eli5: The examples show the bandwidth number shrinking as bigger boxes get booked, like a bus showing fewer big seats the more groups sit down.

sections.title: Scalability and Compatibility
sections.content:
The extension does not introduce OSPF scalability issues and does not change flooding frequency. Only unreserved and MAX LSP Bandwidth for supported priorities are advertised, and fixed containers advertise a count in 16 bits instead of a bandwidth in 32 bits. Bundling component links with homogeneous hierarchies, as in RFC 4201, is RECOMMENDED to cut the data further.

Implementations MAY also support the advertisement in RFC 4203. If a node supports both methods, it MUST allow configuring which one is followed. The choice is a matter of policy, and lets nodes find peers using the same method.
sections.eli5: The new announcements are kept small so they do not clog the network. Old and new styles can live together, and the operator picks which to use.

sections.title: Security and IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The extension travels in OSPFv2 Opaque LSAs, which are not used for SPF computation or normal routing, so it has no direct effect on IP routing. Tampering with GMPLS TE LSAs could still affect the underlying optical or SONET-SDH transport. The OSPF security mechanisms in RFC 2328 apply as noted in RFC 3630, RFC 6863 analyses OSPF security, and RFC 5920 covers threats.

IANA assigned value 110, OTN-TDM capable, in the GMPLS Signaling Parameters Switching Types registry, and created a new sub-registry for OTN-TDM SCSI sub-TLV types: 0 reserved, 1 fixed containers, 2 flexible containers, with 3 to 65535 unassigned and allocated by Standards Action.
sections.eli5: If someone faked these announcements they could confuse the optical gear, so the usual OSPF protections matter. IANA also keeps the official list of the new numbers.

fields.desc: The ODU type being advertised (values in RFC 7139).

fields.desc: Number of multiplexing stages, matching the Stage fields.

fields.name: T
fields.desc: Set if the signal type can be terminated.

fields.name: S
fields.desc: Set if the signal type can be switched.

fields.name: Priority
fields.desc: Bitmap of advertised priorities, bit 0 leftmost.

items.desc: Interfaces configured for 1.25 Gbps slots only.
